title: Minimax Precision of Pooled Pair Assays with Outcome-Dependent Clinic Revisits
banked_reason: Stage 0.5 (typed) BELOW NOVELTY FLOOR — D0.5.G tier=incremental < floor=field (target=field). Not salvageable within scope — bank downgraded.
gap_reasons: The delivered proofs establish matched adaptive and prespecified-schedule risk and honest-length orders for the same unrestricted clinic-law class, including original-history converses and pathwise budget accounting. The logarithmic-round theorem establishes sufficiency only; the framing does not falsely claim necessity or completion of feedback-round-frontier. The scalar coefficient identity is classical, as confirmed by [Haber–Malinovsky–Albert, Section 6.4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1608.02241), so the contribution rests on screened mixture estimation, hard-budget attainability and the logarithmic design separation. Its breadth remains limited to one singular functional under perfect fixed-pair assays, without a framework covering other latent functionals. The enormous conservative constants and smallest-budget checks provide no evidence of useful finite-budget gains, while the prospective HIV application is remote from the high-prevalence endpoint governing the worst case; these limitations constrain the paper score to 6.4. The published mixed-effects inverse-sampling comparator remains a theorem-text source-verification item: its [accessible abstract](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25601742/) establishes neither a matching theorem nor its absence. [D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 6.4 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'incremental'. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived adaptive risk of order 1/B and globally honest length of order 1/sqrt(B), versus log(e+B)/B and its square root for prespecified revisit schedules, plus logarithmic-round sufficiency. Mathematics and decision panels passed and the classical inverse-binomial source was verified, but the final novelty tier was incremental (score ceiling 6.4 below field gate 7.4), confirmed by an independent main validity gate. The intermediate-round converse remains open, the mixed-effects comparator full text remains unverified, and no F-stage or Lean certification was attempted.
tldr: Outcome-dependent revisits remove a logarithmic precision loss in this pooled-only clinic experiment. For arbitrary joint clinic-prevalence laws and at most \(B\) perfect pair assays on every path, the matched all-controller mean squared error is of order \(B^{-1}\), and the globally honest interval length is of order \(B^{-1/2}\). Prespecified clinic depths instead have matched orders \(\log(e+B)/B\) and \(\sqrt{\log(e+B)/B}\). Explicit round-committed protocols already attain the adaptive frontier whenever \(J\ge\min\{B,1+\lceil\log_2 B\rceil\}\), so \(O(\log(e+B))\) feedback rounds suffice. The residual question is the intermediate regime \(2\le J<1+\lceil\log_2 B\rceil\), including matching converses, necessity of feedback growth, and uniform risk--length comparison.
gap: Classical inverse-binomial prevalence estimation supplies scalar unbiasedness, and heterogeneous-coin algorithms supply feedback arguments for separated or smooth targets. Neither verified result gives the joint risk and global honest-length optimum for an unrestricted square-root clinic mixture under a pathwise assay quota.
fill: The two matched frontiers compare every adaptive controller with every seeded prespecified schedule in the same \(\mathcal F\). The feedback-round question retains that experiment and asks how much delayed interaction preserves the gain.
